q: What is CPT in the hybrid program and how much does the CPT course cost?
answer:
CPT (Curricular Practical Training) lets F-1 students gain work experience related to their major [1]. The hybrid program requires it. Each hybrid student must secure an approved internship or employment and stay continuously enrolled in the CPT course each term [1].

**Cost:** The CPT course fee equals one credit hour of tuition per term [1][3]. The exact dollar amount isn't on these pages. The tuition page says to email gradinternational@belhaven.edu for current rates, and Belhaven may change fees and tuition [3].

For you as an F-1 student:
- Don't start working until you receive a CPT-authorized I-20 [4].
- CPT must relate directly to your program and can't be backdated [4].
- Twelve or more months of full-time CPT at the same degree level makes you ineligible for OPT at that level [4].
- You can travel during CPT but can't work while abroad. You need a travel signature on your I-20 to re-enter [1].

To confirm your own CPT situation, check with the DSO before acting: https://igsupport.belhaven.edu/open.php [7]

Contact: gradinternational@belhaven.edu for tuition rates [3].

- On the main campus schedule, you can drop through Sunday of the first week of classes. After that, dropping counts as a withdrawal, which requires a Blazenet form and can have financial, athletic and academic effects [2].
- For online terms, the 2026-2027 calendar shows drop ends 01/17/2027 for the term starting 01/11/2027. Dropped classes in that window aren't charged. "W" withdrawals run through 02/15/2027 [6]. Check which calendar applies to your program.
- Talk to your academic advisor and financial aid first, since changes can affect aid [2].

Contact the DSO through the ticket link above. For general schedule questions, Student Services is at https://igsupport.belhaven.edu/open.php [1].

q: How do I transfer my SEVIS record to Belhaven?
answer:
As an F-1 student transferring from another U.S. school, you'll use Belhaven's International Student Transfer Eligibility Form. It is required of applicants whose address is in the United States [1].

q: Are accommodations available for online students?
answer:
Yes. Students who qualify under the ADA can request reasonable accommodations through Student Care, which evaluates your documentation [4][3]. The sources don't describe a separate process for online students, so the same Student Care process appears to apply.

What matters for you as an online student:
- Accommodation letters must be renewed each semester you are enrolled, which is the rule for online, adult and grad students [1].
- Professors implement accommodations only after they have the official accommodation letter. Accommodations are not retroactive, so plan ahead [1].
- Your documentation needs a specific DSM-V-TR diagnosis and severity level, the approximate duration, and a description of past services or accommodations. A single test, an IEP or a 504 plan alone isn't sufficient [2].
- Once Student Care has all your information, it reviews your file and contacts you when your letters are ready [1].

The sources don't say whether meetings or document submission can be done remotely. Student Care can confirm that.

Contact Student Care at 601-968-8865 or studentcare@belhaven.edu [7].
